stories.headline: Houthis hit Riyadh tower again; Saudi coalition strikes Yemen's main port
stories.question: A Riyadh tower hit, Yemen's main port struck: is the Gulf war widening?
stories.dek: The Saudi–Houthi truce ended in July, so this fight is not new. What is new is bigger targets: a Riyadh financial tower and Yemen's main port. Meanwhile, Israel raises a possible strike on Iran.

so_far.text: The Houthis are an Iran-aligned group that controls northern Yemen. Saudi Arabia leads a military coalition against them. The Houthis joined the US-Israeli war on Iran on 28 March 2026. An April ceasefire ended major combat, but lower-level fighting continued. In July the Houthis declared their truce with Saudi Arabia over and announced a naval blockade. Full-scale war returned to Yemen in September 2026.

what_happened.text: On 24 November a Houthi strike hit the Public Investment Fund (PIF) tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District. It wounded 11 people: two Saudis, four Egyptians, three Nepalese and two Indians. It was the tower's second hit in under a week. Reports do not say whether a missile or drone struck. On 25 November the Saudi-led coalition said it struck Houthi targets at Hodeidah port, after earlier telling civilians to leave. The Houthis threatened Saudi Red Sea ports, including Jeddah. An unverified report says the Houthis claimed a strike on the Ras Tanura refinery. Separately, Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz said Iran is developing chemical weapons.

steps.text: In July the Houthis ended their truce with Saudi Arabia, removing the rule that had stopped both sides striking each other.
Full-scale war returned in September; in wars without a truce, each strike risks a reply aimed at a more valuable target.
Hitting Riyadh's financial district twice threatens the sense of safety that investors and foreign workers rely on.
Separately, on 25 November the coalition struck Hodeidah, the port that carried about 70% of Yemen's imports and 80% of aid in September 2025.
The Houthis now threaten Jeddah, and Israel's talk of a possible strike on Iran raises the risk of a wider front.

history.text: This chapter starts in April 2022. That month a UN-brokered truce calmed Yemen's war. It largely held until 2026, even after peace talks stalled in 2023. In October 2023 the Houthis began attacking ships at Bab al-Mandab, the narrow southern entrance to the Red Sea. That turned a local war into a shipping crisis. US, UK and Israeli strikes on the Houthis followed in 2024–25. On 28 February 2026 the US and Israel attacked Iran, and the Houthis joined the war on 28 March. An April ceasefire ended major combat, but lower-level fighting went on. The Saudi front broke open in July. After a Mahan Air flight to Sanaa was struck on 13 July, the Houthis declared their ceasefire with Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government finished. On 20 July they announced a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia. After that blockade and strikes on Saudi tankers, full-scale war returned in September. Houthi strikes on southern Saudi cities on 8 September wounded 73 people. On 10 September the Houthis took Mokha and Hays, and on 11 September they claimed the Red Sea coast. One low-confidence tally counts over 2,260 killed in Yemen and 26 killed in Saudi Arabia through 6 November. So the November strikes are a new step in a war that was already running.

lesson.concept: How tit-for-tat strikes climb an escalation ladder
lesson.big_idea: Between armed rivals, each strike invites a reply, and replies often aim higher. A war deepens when targets get bigger. It widens when it reaches new places or new players join.

steps.title: Each strike sends a message
steps.text: Armed rivals pick targets to say: we can hurt you. A remote army post says it quietly. A capital city says it loudly, to the enemy and to its own people.

steps.title: Targets sit on a ladder
steps.text: Think of targets as rungs on a ladder. Low rungs are border posts and bases. Higher rungs are cities, ports, refineries and financial centres. Higher rungs cost more and insult more.

steps.title: Replies tend to climb
steps.text: A side that is hit fears looking weak. So it often replies on the same rung or a higher one. The ladder keeps moving up unless someone steps off.

steps.title: Deeper is not wider
steps.text: A war deepens when it climbs to higher-value targets. It widens when it spreads to new places, or when new countries or groups join. Both can happen together.

steps.title: Truces are the brakes
steps.text: A truce is an agreed rule to stop climbing. Yemen's April 2022 truce largely held until 2026. The Houthis declared their Saudi truce over in July 2026.

example.setup: Imagine two rival neighbours, A and B. Assume each rates targets on a scale of 1 to 5: 1 is a border post, 3 a main port, 5 the capital's financial heart.

lines.label: A strikes first
lines.note: A small message, easy to absorb.

lines.label: B replies higher
lines.note: B fears looking weak, so it climbs.

lines.label: A climbs again
lines.note: Aimed at what B values most.

lines.label: B's choice
lines.calc: Hit back at rung 5, or stop
lines.note: At the top, no rungs remain and costs soar.

lines.label: A new player joins
lines.calc: B's ally attacks A: two fronts
lines.note: Now the war is wider, not just deeper.

example.result: In three moves the fight went from rung 1 to rung 5. That is deepening. Only when the ally joined did it widen. Stepping off the ladder needs a truce or a mediator.

apply.text: Since the truce ended in July, the Saudi–Houthi fight has reached high rungs. In November the Houthis hit Riyadh's financial district, twice in under a week. On 25 November the coalition struck Hodeidah, Yemen's lifeline port, after earlier warning civilians; it is not known if this was a reply. The Houthis now threaten Jeddah. That is mostly deepening. Katz's talk of striking Iran is the possible widening.

practice.q: Suppose B answers A's rung-5 strike by hitting a different city of A's, at rung 3. Did the war deepen, widen, or neither?
practice.answer: Step 1: compare rungs. Rung 3 is below rung 5, so it did not deepen. Step 2: check places. A new city was hit, so the war widened a little. Step 3: check players. No new country joined. So it is wider in place, but not deeper.

check.q: Which development would most clearly WIDEN the war, not just make it more intense?
options: A third Houthi strike on the same Riyadh tower
A new front opening, such as an Israeli strike on Iran
The coalition calling a strike a terrorist attack
check.why: Widening means new places or new players joining. Hitting the same tower again raises intensity; a new country front widens the war.

takeaways: Tit-for-tat strikes climb a ladder: bigger targets deepen a war; new places or players widen it.
The Houthis hit Riyadh's financial tower twice; on 25 November the coalition separately struck Yemen's main port, Hodeidah.

stories.headline: Foreign money lifts Sensex 2,000 points and rupee to eight-month high
stories.question: Why did the Sensex jump 2,000 points and the rupee strengthen, days before the RBI meets?
stories.dek: Record foreign buying and cheaper oil pushed up shares and the rupee on 25 November. A stronger rupee also eases one pressure on the RBI, which meets on 2–4 December.

so_far.text: Prices in India rose through autumn 2026. October consumer inflation was 6.09%, above the RBI's 2–6% band for the first time in two years. The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee, which sets the repo rate, has already raised it to 5.50%. In October SBI Research wanted a 50 bps hike in December. On 13 November it said the odds had 'decisively shifted' to 25 bps. Markets fell sharply on Monday 23 November and were shut on 24 November for Guru Nanak Jayanti.

what_happened.text: On 25 November 2026 the Sensex rose about 2,030 points (2.33%) to near 84,468 by 11:45 am IST. The Nifty rose about 558 points to near 25,907. At the peak the Sensex was up 2,062.22 points, at 84,498.21. Both later gave back some gains but stayed higher. Reports credited record foreign buying of about ₹1.27 lakh crore in November, gains in HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Infosys, Bajaj Finance and Axis Bank, Brent crude near $90 and better earnings sentiment. The rupee closed at 92.23 per dollar, an eight-month high. The same day, the RBI Bulletin said growth was on track.

steps.text: Foreign funds bought a record ₹1.27 lakh crore of Indian shares in November, lifting HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Infosys.
To buy those shares, they swap dollars for rupees, which raises demand for rupees and strengthens it.
Falling crude prices mean importers need fewer dollars, easing pressure on the rupee, Reuters and ET report.
With inflation, rupee and global pressures easing, SBI Research sees a 25 bps hike as enough, not 50.
The RBI's 25 November Bulletin says exports, GST collections, returning foreign flows and earnings keep growth on track.

history.text: The Reserve Bank of India began work on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act of 1934. On 1 January 1949 it was nationalised, meaning the government took ownership. In July 1991, during a balance-of-payments crisis, when India ran short of foreign currency to pay its bills, the rupee was devalued. That showed how much the rupee depends on dollars coming in. In 2016 the RBI Act was amended to create a six-member Monetary Policy Committee to set the repo rate: three RBI members, three government appointees, and a casting vote for the governor. In August 2016 the government gave it a target: 4% consumer inflation, within a 2–6% band. That band is why rising prices now push the RBI to act. From June 2026, net foreign portfolio money flowed back into India, though the RBI's October Bulletin called those flows volatile. In October 2026 consumer inflation hit 6.09%, the first breach of the ceiling in two years. In October SBI Research wanted a 50 bps hike; on 13 November it switched to 25 bps.

analogy.text: Think of rupees as entry tickets to India's share market. Foreign funds must buy tickets, paying in dollars, before they can shop. When many arrive at once, tickets get dearer, so each dollar buys fewer rupees. Oil importers selling rupees to get dollars push the other way.
analogy.breaks: Unlike a ticket booth, the RBI can step in to buy or sell dollars, and foreign money can leave quickly.

for_you.text: Things you pay for in dollars, such as imported gadgets, foreign travel or overseas fees, get slightly cheaper: the rupee went from about 93.88 per dollar on 5 November to 92.23 on 25 November, so each dollar costs fewer rupees. Loans are the other side. If the RBI hikes in December, banks could pass it on, making repo-linked home loans costlier. No EMI figures are available yet.

lesson.concept: How foreign money and oil move the rupee
lesson.big_idea: An exchange rate is a price: how many rupees one dollar costs. When more people want rupees, that price falls and the rupee gets stronger, making imports cheaper.

steps.title: A rate is a price
steps.text: The exchange rate is how many rupees one dollar costs. Fewer rupees per dollar means a stronger rupee. On 25 November it was 92.23, down from about 93.88 on 5 November.

steps.title: Foreign buyers need rupees
steps.text: A foreign fund holding dollars must swap them for rupees before buying Indian shares. More funds swapping means more demand for rupees, which pushes the rupee up. November's foreign buying was a record, about ₹1.27 lakh crore.

steps.title: Oil pulls the other way
steps.text: Crude oil is paid for in dollars, so buyers sell rupees to get dollars. When crude prices fall, they need fewer dollars, and that pressure on the rupee eases.

steps.title: Stronger rupee, cheaper imports
steps.text: Anything priced in dollars now costs fewer rupees. Cheaper imports can ease inflation, one of the pressures SBI Research says has eased before the RBI's December meeting.

apply.text: On 25 November, record November foreign buying of about ₹1.27 lakh crore meant steady demand for rupees, and falling crude cut demand for dollars. The rupee closed at 92.23, an eight-month high. Like the laptop in our example, imports got cheaper in rupees. That easing of pressures is part of why SBI Research says a 25 bps hike is enough.

practice.q: Suppose the rupee weakens to 94 per dollar. What would the same $1,000 laptop cost, and how does it compare with 25 November?
practice.answer: Cost = $1,000 × 94 = ₹94,000. On 25 November it was ₹92,230. ₹94,000 − ₹92,230 = ₹1,770 more. More rupees per dollar means a weaker rupee and dearer imports.

stories.headline: Khalid and Imam denied interim bail; pleas sent to Chief Justice
stories.question: Will Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam finally get bail after years in jail without trial?
stories.dek: Not yet. On 25 November 2026 the Supreme Court refused interim bail and sent the matter to the Chief Justice to set up a three-judge bench. The core question: can long delay beat UAPA's strict bail rule?

so_far.text: In February 2020, riots broke out in northeast Delhi during protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) and the National Register of Citizens (NRC). The riots killed 53 people. Police registered a 'larger conspiracy' case, FIR 59/2020, under the UAPA, India's main anti-terror law. Umar Khalid was arrested in this case on 13 September 2020. Sharjeel Imam is a co-accused. On 5 January 2026 the Supreme Court refused bail to both men. It granted bail to five other co-accused.

what_happened.text: On 25 November 2026 the Supreme Court took up fresh bail pleas from Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam. The bench was Chief Justice of India Surya Kant with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana. It issued notice to Delhi Police, which means it formally asked the police to reply. It refused interim bail, or temporary release, before hearing the police. The bench said the matter goes to the Chief Justice to set up a three-judge bench. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal argued that Khalid has spent over six years in custody. No next hearing date has been reported.

steps.text: Khalid and Imam are charged under UAPA. Its Section 43D(5) bars bail if the accusation looks prima facie true.
At the bail stage, courts read the police case at face value. They do not test the evidence.
The police case paints both men as central planners, so courts have repeatedly found the bar applies.
Najeeb lets long delay justify bail. But in January 2026 the Court said delay gives way if the case looks true.
Lower courts say they are bound by the Supreme Court's order, so the fresh pleas went back there.

history.text:
The story begins with the February 2020 riots in northeast Delhi, during protests against the CAA and NRC. The riots killed 53 people. The police case calls the violence a planned 'larger conspiracy'. Khalid was arrested on 13 September 2020. He faces charges under UAPA sections 13, 16, 17 and 18 and the Arms Act. He also faces IPC charges including rioting, murder and promoting enmity.

Two earlier Supreme Court rulings set the bail rules. Watali (2019) said a UAPA bail judge only checks whether the prosecution's material looks true at first sight. Najeeb (2021) said long delay can still justify bail from a constitutional court.

The sessions court in Karkardooma refused Khalid bail in March 2022. The Delhi High Court refused on 18 October 2022. His 2023 Supreme Court appeal was adjourned again and again, and he withdrew it on 14 February 2024. The sessions court refused him again on 28 May 2024.

On 2 September 2025 the High Court refused bail to Khalid, Imam and others. It said delay alone was not enough. On 5 January 2026 the Supreme Court also refused the two and called them 'ideological drivers'. But it freed five co-accused. It said the two could seek bail again after protected witnesses were examined, or one year from that order. Then the trial court (4 July 2026) and the High Court (30 September 2026) both said they were bound by that order. That left only the Supreme Court.

analogy.text: Ordinary bail is like a door left open unless the police show a good reason to shut it. UAPA bail is a door that stays shut if the police file, read at face value, looks believable. Long delay is a spare key. But in January 2026 the Court said the key does not turn if the file looks strong.

for_you.text: For most readers there is no direct effect on prices, jobs or savings. But the rule at stake applies to anyone charged under UAPA: bail is barred if the police case looks true at first sight. A ruling by three judges would guide smaller benches in other UAPA cases. It is not yet known whether this bench will rule on the delay question.

lesson.concept: How bail works under India's anti-terror law UAPA
lesson.big_idea: In ordinary cases, an accused awaiting trial can often get bail. Under UAPA, a court must refuse bail if the police case looks true at first sight. Long delay helps, but not automatically.

steps.title: Bail in ordinary cases
steps.text: Bail means release from jail while the trial goes on. In ordinary criminal cases, courts often treat bail as the norm, because the accused has not been convicted.

steps.title: UAPA flips the test
steps.text: Under UAPA, Section 43D(5) says a court must refuse bail if it finds the accusation prima facie true, meaning true at first sight. Khalid and Imam face UAPA charges.

steps.title: The judge reads, not tests
steps.text: In Watali (2019), the Supreme Court said UAPA bail judges only check whether the prosecution's material is prima facie true. Weighing the evidence properly is left to the trial.

steps.title: Delay as a safety valve
steps.text: In Najeeb (2021), the Court held that Section 43D(5) does not stop constitutional courts, meaning the High Courts and Supreme Court, from granting bail for long delay.

steps.title: But delay is not automatic
steps.text: A January 2026 report says the Court held Najeeb does not mechanically override Section 43D(5). Delay triggers closer scrutiny, but gives way if the case looks prima facie true.

example.setup: Imagine two people, Asha and Ravi, charged in the same UAPA case. Both have spent four years in jail, and the trial is not finished.

lines.label: Which law?
lines.note: The special UAPA bail test replaces the ordinary one.

lines.label: Read the police file
lines.calc: Asha: called the planner. Ravi: attended one meeting
lines.note: The judge takes the file at face value, without testing it.

lines.label: Prima facie test
lines.calc: Asha: looks true. Ravi: looks weak
lines.note: The bar clearly applies to Asha; for Ravi it is doubtful.

lines.label: Add the delay
lines.calc: Four years each (assume), trial not finished
lines.note: Long delay prompts a closer look for both.

lines.label: Outcome
lines.calc: Ravi gets bail; Asha stays in jail
lines.note: Delay alone does not beat a strong prima facie case.

example.result: Same law, same delay, different results. What decides it is how central each person looks in the police case, not just how long they have waited.

apply.text: On 5 January 2026 the Supreme Court read the police case and called Khalid and Imam prima facie central 'ideological drivers', like Asha in our example. So the bar held despite years in jail, while five others got bail. On 25 November 2026 Kapil Sibal again stressed Khalid's six-plus years in custody. The matter now goes to the Chief Justice to set up a three-judge bench.

practice.q: Suppose Asha has now spent eight years in jail, and the police file still calls her the planner. Under the January 2026 reading, does delay alone get her bail?
practice.answer: Step 1: it is a UAPA case, so Section 43D(5) applies. Step 2: the file calls her the planner, so the case looks prima facie true. Step 3: eight years of delay triggers closer scrutiny under Najeeb. Step 4: under the January 2026 reading, delay gives way to the threshold. So no, not by delay alone.

stories.headline: Huang's return and Dell's record fail to stop the AI slide
stories.question: Nvidia has Huang back and Dell posted a record quarter, so why are AI stocks still falling?
stories.dek: The good news helped only briefly. Reports point to lasting fears over the AI boom, growing worries about Big Tech borrowing to pay for AI, and new tariff threats.

so_far.text: AI stocks have been falling since early November 2026. On 6 November Asian shares fell after the Nasdaq, the main US tech index, entered a correction. A correction is a fall of 10% or more from a peak. On 17 November South Korea's Kospi fell below 5,000 for the first time in nine months. Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resigned after reports of extramarital affairs. One involved a former executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer under US investigation. On 19 November Anthropic listed at $83 a share.

what_happened.text: On Monday 23 November 2026 Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. It said senior US officials had assured it that he posed no national security risk. Donald Trump backed his return, and Senator Elizabeth Warren called it 'reckless'. Nvidia shares jumped nearly 32%, their best day since May 2003. The rally faded on 24 November. Nvidia fell about 6%, the Nasdaq lost 1.48%, and Anthropic closed at $81.91, below its IPO price. Dell's shares rose after it reported that quarterly revenue had more than doubled to $54.94bn. On 25 November Asian tech stocks fell sharply.

steps.text: Huang's return sent Nvidia up nearly 32%, but the BBC's Faisal Islam wrote that fears over the AI boom had not gone away.
Dell's and Nvidia's sales are Big Tech's AI spending, and Big Tech is paying for part of it by borrowing.
Lenders now want more: the risk premium on tech bonds rose from 0.76 to 1.08 percentage points.
CNBC reported growing AI debt worries and said Nvidia's rebound masked a Big Tech spending squeeze.
Reuters tied the renewed fall on 25 November to both AI worries and new tariff threats.

history.text:
Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led it ever since. The AI chip boom made it a giant. Its market value passed $2 trillion in March 2024 and $3 trillion in June 2024. On 29 October 2025 it became the first public company worth $5 trillion.

The boom carried a worry. By November 2025 investors feared that US tech giants were borrowing heavily to pay for AI. A Reuters analysis said those worries would grow as the tech giants flooded the bond market. Investors also worried about 'circular financing', because Nvidia was investing in its own customers, such as OpenAI. Michael Burry disclosed a short, which is a bet that Nvidia's shares would fall. Kospi fell nearly 4% on 21 November 2025.

The borrowing kept growing. In June 2026 Nvidia sold about $25bn of bonds, its first bond sale since 2021. In July 2026 Fortune reported that the dollar bond market was saturated with AI debt. In November 2026 Oracle sold $10bn of bonds, Microsoft sold $25bn and Alphabet sold €6bn. Lenders began charging tech firms more. Then Huang resigned. Capital Economics said Anthropic's listing 'has failed to rekindle enthusiasm for tech stocks'.

lesson.concept: How borrowing costs shape the AI spending bet
lesson.big_idea: AI sales at Nvidia and Dell are Big Tech's spending, and Big Tech pays for part of it with borrowed money. When lenders charge more, that spending must earn more to pay off, so investors can grow cautious.

steps.title: Sales are someone's spending
steps.text: When a tech giant buys AI servers, that money becomes Dell's or Nvidia's revenue. So record sales for the sellers mean record spending by the buyers. Big Tech pays for part of this spending by borrowing.

steps.title: Borrowing through bonds
steps.text: A bond is a loan from investors. The company pays interest every year and repays the full amount later. In November 2026 Microsoft sold $25bn of bonds and Oracle sold $10bn.

steps.title: Interest = safe rate + premium
steps.text: Lenders charge roughly what a safe government bond pays, plus a risk premium. That premium is extra pay for lending to a riskier firm. On tech bonds it rose from 0.76 to 1.08 percentage points.

steps.title: Costlier loans raise the bar
steps.text: Higher interest means each data centre must earn more just to cover its loan. If investors doubt it will, they value the spenders' shares lower. The sellers' shares can fall too.

example.setup: Say a tech company borrows $10bn to build AI data centres. Assume the safe government rate is 4%, and use the two risk premiums above.

example.result: The same project now costs $32m more each year. Its data centres must earn more than 5.08% a year, not 4.76%, just to cover the loan.

apply.text: This helps explain the worry in the news. The tech risk premium rose to 1.08 points, and S&P turned Meta's outlook negative over its AI spending. CNBC said AI debt worries were growing and that Nvidia's rebound masked a Big Tech spending squeeze. Reuters tied the 25 November fall to AI worries and tariff threats.

practice.q: Use the same assumed 4% safe rate. This time the company borrows $25bn, the size of Microsoft's November bond sale. How much extra interest does it pay each year?
practice.answer: At the old rate of 4.76%, interest is 4.76% of $25bn = $1.19bn. At the new rate of 5.08%, it is 5.08% of $25bn = $1.27bn. Extra: $1.27bn − $1.19bn = $80m a year. Shortcut: the premium rose 0.32 points, and 0.32% of $25bn = $80m.

stories.headline: Two billion logins left open as hackers breach a CIA system
stories.question: Two billion logins leaked and the CIA hacked: how exposed is your data?
stories.dek: An open database held about 2 billion logins from unknown sources, likely multiple breaches. Your risk depends on whether you reuse passwords, not the headline number. An unclassified CIA system was also breached.

so_far.text: You need two facts to follow this story. First, infostealers are malware that copy passwords and other data from an infected device into text files. Those files are given away on Telegram or sold on cybercrime markets. Second, huge 'leaks' are often compilations of old data. A reported leak of 16 billion credentials in June 2025 was not a new breach. This story also continues a run of hacks. On 19 November 2026 Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirmed breaches at outside vendors, claimed by the gang n0n. The European Commission called an attack it detected on 22 October AI-generated.

what_happened.text: On 24 November 2026, Engadget and 9to5Mac reported two exposed databases. Researcher Jeremiah Fowler found one with about 2 billion login credentials and no password or encryption. It also held roughly 400,000 documents that appear to come from advanced malware, sorted into one folder per victim. UpGuard's Greg Pollock found another with over 1.6 billion mostly Chinese documents, including at least 840 million national ID numbers. Nobody knows who owned either database. The same day, The New York Times reported that hackers breached an unclassified open-source intelligence system shared by the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI). A source says classified networks were not involved and the problem is resolved.

steps.text: Infostealer malware on a person's device copies saved passwords and other data into text files called logs.
These logs and old breach data are shared or sold, and some people merge many leaks into giant databases.
This database, likely drawn from multiple breaches, sat on a server with no password or encryption, so anyone could read it.
A leaked password opens every account where it was reused, and a stolen cookie can even skip the login.
The FBI's crime database was also hit that day; no link to the CIA breach is shown, and officials say US outages don't look coordinated.

history.text: Big data leaks are not new, but they have changed shape over the years. First came giant breaches of single companies. Yahoo's break-ins of 2012 to 2014 were disclosed in 2017. They hit all three billion of its accounts and exposed names, emails, birth dates and phone numbers. India had its own cases. In 2018 a database of Aadhaar identity and biometric data on 1.1 billion people was reportedly sold by criminals. A 2023 breach reportedly affected 815 million Indians. Data on 533 million Facebook users, from 2019, was posted on a hacking forum and reported in 2021. Next came careless storage. In 2020 a misconfigured server at the adult site CAM4 exposed 11 billion records, and nobody had to break in. Then came compilations. In July 2024 RockYou2024, a forum post of 9,948,575,739 unique passwords, simply stitched together past leaks. It built on an earlier list called RockYou2021. In June 2025 BleepingComputer said a reported '16 billion credentials' leak was also old data. Alongside all this, infostealer malware copies logins straight from infected devices, and its logs are given away or sold. The database reported on 24 November 2026 echoes these patterns. Its logins come from unknown sources, likely multiple breaches. It also held about 400,000 documents that appear to come from advanced malware. And it sat on an open server with no password.

for_you.text: The coverage does not mention India, Aadhaar or PAN, and the ID database is mainly Chinese. But the logins span dozens of countries, so Indian accounts cannot be ruled out. lesson.concept: How leaked logins get used against you
lesson.big_idea: A leaked password is dangerous on every site where you reused it, because attackers try it everywhere. Unique passwords limit a leak to one account, and a second factor stops the password working alone.

steps.title: A leak hands over a pair
steps.text: Most logins are an email plus a password. When a site is breached or a device infected, that pair lands in a list. Infostealer logs often save it as website, username and password.

steps.title: Attackers try the pair everywhere
steps.text: Criminals use software to test a leaked pair on many other sites. This is called credential stuffing. It only works on accounts where you reused the same password.

steps.title: Stolen cookies skip the password
steps.text: Browser cookies are the small files that keep you logged in. Malware on a device can copy them too. A stolen cookie can let someone into an account without the password at all.

steps.title: Unique passwords contain the damage
steps.text: If each account has its own password, one leak opens only one account. A password manager creates and remembers them for you, so this is practical.

steps.title: A second factor blocks the password
steps.text: Two-factor authentication also asks for a code. Codes from an authenticator app are safer than SMS, which SIM-swap fraud can hijack. Passkeys replace typed passwords altogether.

example.setup: Say Ravi uses one password on five accounts: email, shopping, social media, a food app and a game. The game site is breached, and his email and password leak.

lines.label: The leak
lines.note: It comes from the game site only.

lines.label: Attackers try it
lines.calc: Same pair tested on all 5 sites
lines.note: Software does this automatically; this is credential stuffing.

lines.label: One shared password
lines.note: Every account accepts the leaked password.

lines.label: Unique passwords
lines.note: Only the game account's password leaked.

lines.label: Plus app two-factor
lines.note: Attackers also need a code from Ravi's phone.

example.result: Reuse turned one leak into five lost accounts. Unique passwords cut that to one. A second factor made even that password useless on its own, unless his cookies were also stolen.

apply.text: The new database held password and cookie folders for each victim, with logins spanning dozens of countries. Its sources are unknown, likely multiple breaches. If your password is in it and you reuse it, every account sharing it is exposed, like Ravi's five. That is why the coverage advises unique passwords, authenticator-app two-factor and passkeys.

practice.q: Meera reuses one password on 8 accounts and has unique passwords on 4 others. The shared password leaks. How many accounts open by password alone?
practice.answer: The shared password works on all 8 accounts that use it. The 4 unique ones stay shut, because their passwords did not leak. So 8 of 12 are open. If she adds app-based two-factor to 6 of those 8, only 8 − 6 = 2 open by password alone.

check.why: Attackers try a leaked pair everywhere. Unique passwords stop it spreading, and a second factor blocks password-only logins. Copies of the data may already exist.

scenes.say: 24 November 2026 ko news outlets ne researcher Jeremiah Fowler ki khoj report ki: kareeb 2 billion login credentials, bina password aur bina encryption ke. Inka source pata nahi hai, shayad yeh kai breaches se aaye hain. Is database mein kareeb 4 lakh documents bhi the, jo advanced malware se aaye lagte hain. Har victim ka ek alag folder.
scenes.speak: 24 November 2026 को news outlets ने researcher Jeremiah Fowler की खोज report की: करीब 2 billion login credentials, बिना password और बिना encryption के। इनका source पता नहीं है, शायद ये कई breaches से आए हैं। इस database में करीब 4 लाख documents भी थे, जो advanced malware से आए लगते हैं। हर victim का एक अलग folder।

scenes.say: Ek doosra database, jise UpGuard ke Greg Pollock ne dhoondha, usmein ek point chhe billion se zyada documents the, zyaadatar Chinese. Inmein kam se kam 840 million national ID numbers hain. Dono databases ka maalik kaun tha, kisi ko nahi pata. Engadget kehta hai dono hata diye gaye. Lekin 9to5Mac logins wale database ke liye yeh confirm nahi karta.
scenes.speak: एक दूसरा database, जिसे UpGuard के Greg Pollock ने ढूंढा, उसमें एक point छह billion से ज़्यादा documents थे, ज़्यादातर Chinese। इनमें कम से कम 840 million national ID numbers हैं। दोनों databases का मालिक कौन था, किसी को नहीं पता। Engadget कहता है दोनों हटा दिए गए। लेकिन 9to5Mac logins वाले database के लिए यह confirm नहीं करता।

scenes.say: Usi din The New York Times ne report kiya ki hackers ek unclassified intelligence system mein ghus gaye. Yeh system CIA aur Office of the Director of National Intelligence share karte hain. Yeh public sources se jaankari jutata hai. Ek source ke mutabik classified networks shaamil nahi the, aur problem resolve ho chuki hai.
scenes.show: CIA system breached; classified networks safe
scenes.speak: उसी दिन The New York Times ने report किया कि hackers एक unclassified intelligence system में घुस गए। यह system CIA और Office of the Director of National Intelligence share करते हैं। यह public sources से जानकारी जुटाता है। एक source के मुताबिक classified networks शामिल नहीं थे, और problem resolve हो चुकी है।

scenes.say: Yahan tak pahunche kaise? Shuruaat hoti hai bade breaches se. Yahoo mein 2012 se 2014 tak break-ins hue, jo 2017 mein disclose hue, aur saare 3 billion accounts par asar pada. 2018 mein, reports ke mutabik, criminals ne ek point ek billion logon ka Aadhaar data becha.
scenes.show: From single breaches to giant compilations
scenes.speak: यहाँ तक पहुँचे कैसे? शुरुआत होती है बड़े breaches से। Yahoo में 2012 से 2014 तक break-ins हुए, जो 2017 में disclose हुए, और सारे 3 billion accounts पर असर पड़ा। 2018 में, reports के मुताबिक, criminals ने एक point एक billion लोगों का Aadhaar data बेचा।

timeline.what: Yahoo: all 3 billion accounts hit
Aadhaar data on 1.1 billion reportedly sold
CAM4 server exposes 11 billion records
RockYou2024: 9.95 billion old passwords
'16 billion' leak is old data
2 billion logins left open

scenes.say: 2023 ke ek breach ne reportedly 815 million Indians ko affect kiya. 533 million Facebook users ka data ek hacking forum par daala gaya. Phir aayi laaparwah storage. 2020 mein CAM4 naam ki site ke ek misconfigured server ne 11 billion records expose kar diye.
scenes.speak: 2023 के एक breach ने reportedly 815 million Indians को affect किया। 533 million Facebook users का data एक hacking forum पर डाला गया। फिर आई लापरवाह storage। 2020 में CAM4 नाम की site के एक misconfigured server ने 11 billion records expose कर दिए।

scenes.say: Phir aaye compilations. July 2024 mein RockYou2024 ne nau point nau paanch billion passwords post kiye, jo purane leaks ko jodkar bane the. June 2025 ka 16 billion wala leak bhi purana data tha. Naya database bhi aisa hi hai: unknown sources se logins, shayad kai breaches se, ek khule server par pade hue.
scenes.speak: फिर आए compilations। July 2024 में RockYou2024 ने नौ point नौ पाँच billion passwords post किए, जो पुराने leaks को जोड़कर बने थे। June 2025 का 16 billion वाला leak भी पुराना data था। नया database भी ऐसा ही है: unknown sources से logins, शायद कई breaches से, एक खुले server पर पड़े हुए।

scenes.say: Yeh hacks ke ek silsile ki agli kadi bhi hai. 19 November ko Chase, Visa aur Mastercard ne bahar ke vendors par breaches confirm kiye, jinka daava n0n naam ke gang ne kiya. Aur European Commission ne 22 October ko pakde gaye ek attack ko AI-generated bataya.
scenes.speak: यह hacks के एक सिलसिले की अगली कड़ी भी है। 19 November को Chase, Visa और Mastercard ने बाहर के vendors पर breaches confirm किए, जिनका दावा n0n नाम के gang ने किया। और European Commission ने 22 October को पकड़े गए एक attack को AI-generated बताया।

scenes.say: Toh logins itne bade scale par leak kyun hote hain? Pehla, infostealer naam ka malware kisi ke device ko infect karta hai. Yeh saved passwords aur baaki data ko text files mein copy karta hai, jinhe logs kehte hain. Doosra, yeh logs aur purana breach data Telegram par share hota hai ya bikta hai. Kuch log kai leaks ko jodkar giant databases bana dete hain.
scenes.show: Infostealer: malware that copies your logins
scenes.speak: तो logins इतने बड़े scale पर leak क्यों होते हैं? पहला, infostealer नाम का malware किसी के device को infect करता है। यह saved passwords और बाकी data को text files में copy करता है, जिन्हें logs कहते हैं। दूसरा, ये logs और पुराना breach data Telegram पर share होता है या बिकता है। कुछ लोग कई leaks को जोड़कर giant databases बना देते हैं।

scenes.say: Teesra, yeh database, jo shayad kai breaches se bana tha, ek aise server par tha jis par koi password nahi tha. Jisne bhi dhoondha, woh padh sakta tha. Chautha, leak hua password har us account ko khol deta hai jahan aapne wahi password repeat kiya. Aur chori hui cookie, yaani woh file jo aapko logged in rakhti hai, login ko skip bhi kar sakti hai.
scenes.speak: तीसरा, यह database, जो शायद कई breaches से बना था, एक ऐसे server पर था जिस पर कोई password नहीं था। जिसने भी ढूंढा, वो पढ़ सकता था। चौथा, leak हुआ password हर उस account को खोल देता है जहाँ आपने वही password repeat किया। और चोरी हुई cookie, यानी वो file जो आपको logged in रखती है, login को skip भी कर सकती है।

scenes.say: Paanchva, US ke hacks. Android Headlines ke mutabik, CIA breach wale din hi attackers ne FBI ke National Crime Information Center ko bhi nishana banaya. Dono ke beech koi link ab tak saamne nahi aaya. Officials kehte hain US mein outages ka yeh bada silsila ek coordinated attack jaisa nahi lagta.
scenes.show: FBI also hit; no link shown
scenes.speak: पाँचवाँ, US के hacks। Android Headlines के मुताबिक, CIA breach वाले दिन ही attackers ने FBI के National Crime Information Center को भी निशाना बनाया। दोनों के बीच कोई link अब तक सामने नहीं आया। Officials कहते हैं US में outages का यह बड़ा सिलसिला एक coordinated attack जैसा नहीं लगता।

scenes.say: Ab players ki baat. Black Hills Information Security ke Jeremiah Fowler ne logins database dhoondha. UpGuard ke Greg Pollock ne Chinese documents dhoondhe. Breach hua system CIA aur intelligence director ka office share karte hain. Kisi culprit ka naam nahi liya gaya. Sirf Nextgov kehta hai ki maana ja raha hai ARTEX naam ka AI tool use hua.
scenes.show: Who found it, who was hit
scenes.image: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
scenes.speak: अब players की बात। Black Hills Information Security के Jeremiah Fowler ने logins database ढूंढा। UpGuard के Greg Pollock ने Chinese documents ढूंढे। Breach हुआ system CIA और intelligence director का office share करते हैं। किसी culprit का नाम नहीं लिया गया। सिर्फ Nextgov कहता है कि माना जा रहा है ARTEX नाम का AI tool use हुआ।

players.name: Greg Pollock
players.role: UpGuard; found the Chinese documents database

scenes.say: Yeh logins darjanon deshon mein faile hain. Estimates ke mutabik 114 million se zyada Google accounts, 88 million Facebook, kareeb 42 million Roblox, chhattees point chhe million Amazon, aur lagbhag 33 million X accounts hain. Kuch overlap ho sakte hain.
scenes.speak: ये logins दर्जनों देशों में फैले हैं। Estimates के मुताबिक 114 million से ज़्यादा Google accounts, 88 million Facebook, करीब 42 million Roblox, छत्तीस point छह million Amazon, और लगभग 33 million X accounts हैं। कुछ overlap हो सकते हैं।

scenes.say: Ab purane leaks se compare kijiye. 2 billion, RockYou2024 ka lagbhag paanchva hissa hai. Yahoo mein 3 billion accounts hit hue the. CAM4 ne 11 billion records expose kiye the. Yeh ginti alag alag cheezein naapti hai, isliye sirf mote taur par compare kijiye.
scenes.show: 2 billion: big, but not the biggest
scenes.speak: अब पुराने leaks से compare कीजिए। 2 billion, RockYou2024 का लगभग पाँचवाँ हिस्सा है। Yahoo में 3 billion accounts hit हुए थे। CAM4 ने 11 billion records expose किए थे। ये गिनती अलग अलग चीज़ें नापती है, इसलिए सिर्फ मोटे तौर पर compare कीजिए।

scenes.say: Ab woh ek idea jo seekhna hai: leak hue logins aapke khilaaf kaise use hote hain. Zyaadatar logins ek email aur ek password hote hain. Jab koi site breach hoti hai ya device infect hota hai, toh yeh jodi ek list mein pahunch jaati hai. Attackers software se ise kai doosri sites par try karte hain. Isi ko credential stuffing kehte hain.
scenes.show: Credential stuffing: one pair, many sites
scenes.speak: अब वो एक idea जो सीखना है: leak हुए logins आपके खिलाफ कैसे use होते हैं। ज़्यादातर logins एक email और एक password होते हैं। जब कोई site breach होती है या device infect होता है, तो यह जोड़ी एक list में पहुँच जाती है। Attackers software से इसे कई दूसरी sites पर try करते हैं। इसी को credential stuffing कहते हैं।

scenes.say: Yeh sirf wahin kaam karta hai jahan aapne password repeat kiya. Chori hui cookie aur aage jaati hai: bina kisi password ke andar ghus sakti hai. Aapka bachaav? Har account ka alag password, aur password manager ise aasaan bana deta hai. Phir two-factor login lagaiye. Authenticator apps SMS codes se behtar hain, kyunki SIM-swap fraud SMS codes ko hijack kar sakta hai. Passkeys isse bhi aage hain.
scenes.speak: यह सिर्फ वहीं काम करता है जहाँ आपने password repeat किया। चोरी हुई cookie और आगे जाती है: बिना किसी password के अंदर घुस सकती है। आपका बचाव? हर account का अलग password, और password manager इसे आसान बना देता है। फिर two-factor login लगाइए। Authenticator apps SMS codes से बेहतर हैं, क्योंकि SIM-swap fraud SMS codes को hijack कर सकता है। Passkeys इससे भी आगे हैं।

scenes.say: Maan lijiye Ravi 5 accounts par ek hi password use karta hai. Ek game site se woh leak ho jaata hai. Attackers wahi jodi paanchon par try karte hain. Ek shared password ho, toh paanchon khul jaate hain. Alag alag passwords hon, toh sirf game account khulta hai. App-based two-factor jod dein, toh akela password ek bhi account nahi kholta. Bas tab tak, jab tak uski cookies bhi chori na hui hon.
scenes.speak: मान लीजिए Ravi 5 accounts पर एक ही password use करता है। एक game site से वो leak हो जाता है। Attackers वही जोड़ी पाँचों पर try करते हैं। एक shared password हो, तो पाँचों खुल जाते हैं। अलग अलग passwords हों, तो सिर्फ game account खुलता है। App-based two-factor जोड़ दें, तो अकेला password एक भी account नहीं खोलता। बस तब तक, जब तक उसकी cookies भी चोरी न हुई हों।

scenes.say: Ek aam myth hai: 2 billion matlab 2 billion naye victims. Lekin aksar in ginti mein purana data aur overlapping accounts dohraaye jaate hain. India ki baat karein toh coverage mein India, Aadhaar ya PAN ka zikr nahi hai, aur ID database mainly Chinese hai. Par logins darjanon deshon ke hain, isliye Indian accounts hone se inkaar nahi kiya ja sakta.
scenes.show: Indian accounts can't be ruled out
scenes.speak: एक आम myth है: 2 billion मतलब 2 billion नए victims। लेकिन अक्सर इन गिनती में पुराना data और overlapping accounts दोहराए जाते हैं। India की बात करें तो coverage में India, Aadhaar या PAN का ज़िक्र नहीं है, और ID database mainly Chinese है। पर logins दर्जनों देशों के हैं, इसलिए Indian accounts होने से इनकार नहीं किया जा सकता।

scenes.say: Toh Ravi ki tarah sabak apply kijiye. Database mein har victim ke password aur cookie folders the. Agar aap ek password kai jagah use karte hain, toh har jagah use badaliye. Password manager use kijiye. Two-factor codes ko SMS se authenticator app par shift kijiye, aur passkeys ke baare mein sochiye. Aur phishing messages se savdhaan rahiye, jo aapko phansaane ki koshish karte hain.
scenes.show: Change reused passwords; use an authenticator
scenes.speak: तो Ravi की तरह सबक apply कीजिए। Database में हर victim के password और cookie folders थे। अगर आप एक password कई जगह use करते हैं, तो हर जगह उसे बदलिए। Password manager use कीजिए। Two-factor codes को SMS से authenticator app पर shift कीजिए, और passkeys के बारे में सोचिए। और phishing messages से सावधान रहिए, जो आपको फँसाने की कोशिश करते हैं।

scenes.say: Aage kya dekhna hai? Dono databases ka maalik kaun tha, aur kya logins database sach mein offline hai? Kya Indian accounts ismein hain? CIA system par hamla kisne kiya, kya kuch chori hua, aur kya iska FBI hack se koi link hai? Coverage mein in sawaalon ke jawaab ki koi date nahi di gayi hai.
scenes.speak: आगे क्या देखना है? दोनों databases का मालिक कौन था, और क्या logins database सच में offline है? क्या Indian accounts इसमें हैं? CIA system पर हमला किसने किया, क्या कुछ चोरी हुआ, और क्या इसका FBI hack से कोई link है? Coverage में इन सवालों के जवाब की कोई date नहीं दी गई है।

scenes.say: Teen baatein yaad rakhiye. Leak hua password har us jagah khatarnak hai jahan aapne use repeat kiya, aur second factor sirf password wale logins ko rok deta hai. Kareeb 2 billion logins ka ek khula database saamne aaya, shayad kai breaches se bana, aur ek CIA system breach hua. Ab dekhiye ki data ka maalik kaun tha, Indian accounts ismein hain ya nahi, aur CIA par hamla kisne kiya.
scenes.show: Unique passwords. Second factor. Stay alert.
scenes.speak: तीन बातें याद रखिए। Leak हुआ password हर उस जगह खतरनाक है जहाँ आपने उसे repeat किया, और second factor सिर्फ password वाले logins को रोक देता है। करीब 2 billion logins का एक खुला database सामने आया, शायद कई breaches से बना, और एक CIA system breach हुआ। अब देखिए कि data का मालिक कौन था, Indian accounts इसमें हैं या नहीं, और CIA पर हमला किसने किया।

stories.headline: Pakistan's first astronaut flies on China's rocket; India builds its own
stories.question: Pakistan has its first astronaut in space on a Chinese rocket, so where does India's space programme stand?
stories.dek: Pakistan rode China's spacecraft; it has no rocket or capsule of its own. India builds its own: its navigation system is back to four satellites, and crewed flight is targeted for 2027.

so_far.text: Pakistan has no rocket or crewed spacecraft of its own. It relies on China, its largest trading partner, which has launched Pakistani satellites. In 2024 a Pakistani CubeSat, a small satellite, rode China's Chang'e-6 Moon mission. Two Pakistani pilots, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, trained in Beijing in Mandarin, centrifuge runs and spacecraft systems. ISRO, India's space agency, takes the other road. It builds its own rockets, its own navigation satellites, called NavIC, and its own human spaceflight programme, Gaganyaan.

what_happened.text: On 25 November 2026 China launched Shenzhou-24 from Jiuquan to its Tiangong station. On board were Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, 51, and Wu Yi, 39, and Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, 40, the first foreigner on a Chinese crewed mission. He entered Tiangong the same day. Ali will study cyanobacteria, tiny organisms that make food from sunlight, and return on Shenzhou-23; one analysis puts his stay at about a week. Presidents Xi Jinping and Asif Ali Zardari exchanged congratulatory letters. Mint wrote that the mission highlights Islamabad's dependence on Beijing. On 24 November ISRO chairman V Narayanan said Gaganyaan was 'not delayed', but gave no date.

steps.text: Flying an astronaut needs a rocket and a crew capsule. Pakistan has neither of its own.
So Pakistan took a seat through China: training in Beijing, Chinese hardware, a Chinese launch site, Chinese instructors.
India builds every piece itself, which is slower: Gaganyaan's crewed flight, first targeted for 2021, is now targeted for 2027.
Navigation shows the same pattern: NavIC needs four working satellites, and failures left it at three until NVS-03.

history.text:
India's side of the story begins in 1999. During the Kargil conflict, India asked the US for GPS data, and the US declined. That showed the risk of relying on another country's satellites. In May 2006 the Cabinet approved India's own navigation system, now called NavIC. Its first satellite, IRNSS-1A, launched on 1 July 2013. The first batch of seven was complete by 28 April 2016.

Then the atomic clocks that keep each satellite's time began failing in 2017–18. By May 2018, nine of 21 were offline, and the system weakened. A replacement, NVS-01, launched in May 2023. But NVS-02 failed to reach orbit in January 2025. That left three usable satellites, one short of the four needed for a position fix. On 30 October 2026 a GSLV rocket, on its 20th flight, launched NVS-03 from Sriharikota and restored four.

Human spaceflight came later. Prime Minister Modi announced it on 15 August 2018. On 28 December 2018 the Cabinet approved ₹10,000 crore for a seven-day crewed flight targeted for 2021. That date slipped. An abort test, TV-D1, which checks that a crew can escape a failing rocket, flew on 21 October 2023. On 18 September 2024 the Cabinet raised the budget to ₹20,193 crore and added a module called BAS-01.

Pakistan's path began with China. The idea of a Pakistani crewed flight dates to 2019. In February 2025 the two countries signed the astronaut agreement that led to this flight.

analogy.text: Pakistan has taken a ride in a friend's car. It arrives fast, but the friend owns the car, does the driving and decides the trips. India is building its own car. That takes far longer, but the car, and the decisions, will be India's.
analogy.breaks: Unlike a finished car, India's capsule has not yet flown people; its first uncrewed test flight still has no firm date.

for_you.text: NavIC, India's own navigation system, helps track trains, vehicles and ships, and is linked to the 'one nation, one time' project. With four satellites again, it can give fixes across India and about 1,500 km around. Pakistan's flight changes nothing directly for you. Gaganyaan does involve you: its ₹20,193 crore budget is public money.

misconception.myth: Pakistan now has its own human spaceflight programme, like India's Gaganyaan.
misconception.fact: Pakistan has no launch vehicle or crewed spacecraft. Ali flew on Chinese hardware, from a Chinese site, trained by Chinese instructors.

next.text: Watch for a firm date for Gaganyaan's first uncrewed flight, carrying the robot Vyommitra. ISRO says 'at the earliest opportunity'; one report says not before February 2027. Ali returns on Shenzhou-23. Pakistan's Jinnah-1 rover is due on Chang'e-8 around 2028.

lesson.concept: Why satellite navigation needs four satellites
lesson.big_idea: Your device works out how far it is from each satellite by timing its signal. Three distances fix your place, and a fourth satellite corrects your device's own clock error.

steps.title: Satellites broadcast the time
steps.text: Each navigation satellite carries very precise atomic clocks and keeps sending a signal saying exactly when it was sent. That is why NavIC weakened when its atomic clocks failed in 2017–18.

steps.title: Travel time gives distance
steps.text: Your receiver notes when the signal arrives. Radio signals travel at the speed of light, about 3 lakh km per second. So distance equals that speed times the travel time.

steps.title: Three distances pin your place
steps.text: One distance puts you somewhere on a giant sphere around a satellite. Two spheres overlap in a circle. A third cuts that circle to two points, and only one is near Earth.

steps.title: The fourth fixes the clock
steps.text: Your phone's clock is cheap, not atomic. Its small error spoils every distance. That error is a fourth unknown, so you need a fourth satellite. NavIC had only three usable before NVS-03.

example.setup: Imagine your phone receives a NavIC signal that took 0.07 seconds to arrive. Assume signals travel 3,00,000 km per second, and your phone's clock is off by just 0.001 seconds.

lines.label: Distance to satellite
lines.note: Speed times travel time.

lines.label: Error from clock
lines.note: A one-thousandth-second slip moves you 300 km.

lines.label: Unknowns to solve
lines.note: North-south, east-west, height, and the clock error.

lines.label: Satellites needed
lines.note: Each satellite gives one equation.

lines.label: With only three
lines.note: That was NavIC before 30 October 2026.

example.result: A clock error of one-thousandth of a second throws your position off by 300 km. A fourth satellite lets the receiver work out that error and remove it, which is why four is the minimum.

apply.text: Before NVS-03, NavIC had only three usable satellites, one short of the four needed for a fix. On 30 October 2026 GSLV-F18 put NVS-03 in orbit and restored the minimum. That is why ISRO chairman V Narayanan called NavIC 'a strategic national asset': it is the system India built after the US declined its GPS request in 1999.

practice.q: Your phone's clock is off by 0.002 seconds. Assuming signals travel 3,00,000 km per second, how far off would your position be without a fourth satellite?
practice.answer: Error = speed × clock error. 3,00,000 km/s × 0.002 s = 600 km. Double the clock error, double the distance error. The fourth satellite lets the receiver work out the 0.002 seconds and remove it.

scenes.say: 25 November 2026 ko Pakistan ka pehla astronaut space mein pahuncha, ek Chinese rocket par. Toh India ka apna space programme kahan khada hai? Chaliye samajhte hain.
scenes.show: Pakistan's first astronaut. Where is India?
scenes.speak: 25 November 2026 को Pakistan का पहला astronaut space में पहुँचा, एक Chinese rocket पर। तो India का अपना space programme कहाँ खड़ा है? चलिए समझते हैं।

scenes.say: China ne Jiuquan se Shenzhou 24 launch kiya. Crew mein the Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo aur Wu Yi, aur Pakistan ke 40 saal ke Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. Woh kisi Chinese crewed mission par jaane wale pehle foreigner hain. Usi din woh Tiangong space station mein pahunch gaye.
scenes.show: Shenzhou-24: first foreigner on Chinese crew
scenes.speak: China ने Jiuquan से Shenzhou 24 launch किया। Crew में थे Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo और Wu Yi, और Pakistan के 40 साल के Muhammad Zeeshan Ali। वो किसी Chinese crewed mission पर जाने वाले पहले foreigner हैं। उसी दिन वो Tiangong space station में पहुँच गए।

scenes.say: Ali cyanobacteria ko study karenge. Yeh chhote organisms hain jo sunlight se apna khana banate hain. Crew ka plan 90 se zyada experiments ka hai. Ek analysis ke mutabik Ali lagbhag ek hafta rukenge, aur Shenzhou 23 se wapas aayenge. Presidents Xi Jinping aur Asif Ali Zardari ne ek doosre ko badhai di. Mint ne likha ki isse Islamabad ki Beijing par dependence dikhti hai.
scenes.show: 90+ experiments; Ali stays about a week
scenes.speak: Ali cyanobacteria को study करेंगे। ये छोटे organisms हैं जो sunlight से अपना खाना बनाते हैं। Crew का plan 90 से ज़्यादा experiments का है। एक analysis के मुताबिक Ali लगभग एक हफ़्ता रुकेंगे, और Shenzhou 23 से वापस आएंगे। Presidents Xi Jinping और Asif Ali Zardari ने एक दूसरे को बधाई दी। Mint ने लिखा कि इससे Islamabad की Beijing पर dependence दिखती है।

scenes.say: Aur India? 24 November ko ISRO, yaani India ki space agency, ke head V Narayanan ne kaha ki human spaceflight programme Gaganyaan delay nahi hua hai. Lekin koi date nahi di. Aur 30 October ko ISRO ne ek navigation satellite launch kiya, NVS zero three. Isko yaad rakhiye.
scenes.speak: और India? 24 November को ISRO, यानी India की space agency, के head V Narayanan ने कहा कि human spaceflight programme Gaganyaan delay नहीं हुआ है। लेकिन कोई date नहीं दी। और 30 October को ISRO ने एक navigation satellite launch किया, NVS zero three। इसको याद रखिए।

scenes.say: Wajah samajhne ke liye 1999 mein chaliye. Kargil conflict ke dauraan US ne India ki GPS data ki request thukra di. Toh India ne apna navigation system banaya, jise May 2006 mein approval mila. Pehla satellite 1 July 2013 ko launch hua. April 2016 tak 7 satellites upar the.
scenes.speak: वजह समझने के लिए 1999 में चलिए। Kargil conflict के दौरान US ने India की GPS data की request ठुकरा दी। तो India ने अपना navigation system बनाया, जिसे May 2006 में approval मिला। पहला satellite 1 July 2013 को launch हुआ। April 2016 तक 7 satellites ऊपर थे।

Cabinet approves own navigation system

scenes.say: Phir aayi musibat. Har satellite atomic clocks se time rakhta hai, aur NavIC ki clocks fail hone lagin. May 2018 tak 21 mein se 9 band ho chuki thin. NVS zero one May 2023 mein launch hua, lekin NVS zero two January 2025 mein orbit tak nahi pahuncha. Bache sirf 3 kaam ke satellites. Aur fix ke liye chahiye 4.
scenes.show: Clock failures left NavIC at three
scenes.speak: फिर आई मुसीबत। हर satellite atomic clocks से time रखता है, और NavIC की clocks fail होने लगीं। May 2018 तक 21 में से 9 बंद हो चुकी थीं। NVS zero one May 2023 में launch हुआ, लेकिन NVS zero two January 2025 में orbit तक नहीं पहुँचा। बचे सिर्फ़ 3 काम के satellites। और fix के लिए चाहिए 4।

scenes.say: Human spaceflight baad mein aaya. Prime Minister Modi ne 15 August 2018 ko iska announcement kiya. Usi December Cabinet ne 2021 tak crewed flight ke liye 10000 crore rupaye approve kiye. Woh target khisak gaya. October 2023 mein ek abort test hua, yeh check karne ke liye ki fail hote rocket se crew bach kar nikal sake. September 2024 mein budget badha, aur BAS zero one naam ka module joda gaya.
scenes.speak: Human spaceflight बाद में आया। Prime Minister Modi ने 15 August 2018 को इसका announcement किया। उसी December Cabinet ने 2021 तक crewed flight के लिए 10000 करोड़ रुपये approve किए। वो target खिसक गया। October 2023 में एक abort test हुआ, ये check करने के लिए कि fail होते rocket से crew बच कर निकल सके। September 2024 में budget बढ़ा, और BAS zero one नाम का module जोड़ा गया।

scenes.say: Pakistan ne alag raasta chuna. China ke saath crewed flight ka idea 2019 se hai. 2024 mein ek chhota Pakistani satellite China ke Chang'e 6 Moon mission ke saath gaya. February 2025 mein dono ne astronaut agreement sign kiya. 2 Pakistani pilots ne Beijing mein training li, aur Ali chune gaye.
scenes.speak: Pakistan ने अलग रास्ता चुना। China के साथ crewed flight का idea 2019 से है। 2024 में एक छोटा Pakistani satellite China के Chang'e 6 Moon mission के साथ गया। February 2025 में दोनों ने astronaut agreement sign किया। 2 Pakistani pilots ने Beijing में training ली, और Ali चुने गए।

scenes.say: Toh Pakistan sawaari kyun karta hai, aur India khud kyun banata hai? Astronaut bhejne ke liye rocket aur crew capsule chahiye. Pakistan ke paas inmein se ek bhi nahi hai. Isliye China ne dono diye: Chinese instructors, Chinese hardware, aur Chinese launch site.
scenes.show: No rocket, no capsule: Pakistan rides
scenes.speak: तो Pakistan सवारी क्यों करता है, और India ख़ुद क्यों बनाता है? Astronaut भेजने के लिए rocket और crew capsule चाहिए। Pakistan के पास इनमें से एक भी नहीं है। इसलिए China ने दोनों दिए: Chinese instructors, Chinese hardware, और Chinese launch site।

scenes.say: India har hissa khud banata hai, isliye kaam dheema hai. Jo crewed flight pehle 2021 ke liye target thi, ab uska target 2027 hai. NavIC ki kahani bhi yahi hai: use 4 chalte satellites chahiye, aur failures ki wajah se NVS zero three tak woh 3 par atka tha.
scenes.speak: India हर हिस्सा ख़ुद बनाता है, इसलिए काम धीमा है। जो crewed flight पहले 2021 के लिए target थी, अब उसका target 2027 है। NavIC की कहानी भी यही है: उसे 4 चलते satellites चाहिए, और failures की वजह से NVS zero three तक वो 3 पर अटका था।

scenes.say: Aise sochiye. Pakistan ne dost ki gaadi mein lift li: jaldi pahunch gaye, lekin gaadi dost ki hai aur chala bhi wahi raha hai. India apni gaadi bana raha hai: time lagega, lekin gaadi India ki hogi. Is misaal ki kami: India ke capsule ne abhi tak insaanon ko nahi udaya.
scenes.show: A borrowed ride vs. your own car
scenes.speak: ऐसे सोचिए। Pakistan ने दोस्त की गाड़ी में lift ली: जल्दी पहुँच गए, लेकिन गाड़ी दोस्त की है और चला भी वही रहा है। India अपनी गाड़ी बना रहा है: time लगेगा, लेकिन गाड़ी India की होगी। इस मिसाल की कमी: India के capsule ने अभी तक इंसानों को नहीं उड़ाया।

scenes.say: Ab logon ki baat. Muhammad Zeeshan Ali ek Pakistani pilot hain, aur payload specialist hain, yaani woh crew member jo experiments chalata hai. Khurram Daud ne doosre candidate ke roop mein training li. Pakistan ki space agency Suparco kehti hai ki Ali materials, fluids, life sciences aur biotechnology dekhenge. V Narayanan ISRO ke head hain.
scenes.speak: अब लोगों की बात। Muhammad Zeeshan Ali एक Pakistani pilot हैं, और payload specialist हैं, यानी वो crew member जो experiments चलाता है। Khurram Daud ने दूसरे candidate के रूप में training ली। Pakistan की space agency Suparco कहती है कि Ali materials, fluids, life sciences और biotechnology देखेंगे। V Narayanan ISRO के head हैं।

scenes.say: Sabse zaroori number hai 4. India ke paas ab phir se itne chalte NavIC satellites hain, aur fix ke liye kam se kam itne hi chahiye. NVS zero three se pehle sirf 3 the. GSLV rocket ne 30 October 2026 ko Sriharikota se udaan bhari, yeh uski beesvi flight thi.
scenes.speak: सबसे ज़रूरी number है 4। India के पास अब फिर से इतने चलते NavIC satellites हैं, और fix के लिए कम से कम इतने ही चाहिए। NVS zero three से पहले सिर्फ़ 3 थे। GSLV rocket ने 30 October 2026 को Sriharikota से उड़ान भरी, ये उसकी बीसवीं flight थी।

scenes.say: Gaganyaan ka budget lagbhag double ho gaya hai: 2018 mein 10000 crore rupaye, phir September 2024 mein 20193 crore. Aur isi beech crewed flight ka target 2021 se khisak kar 2027 ho gaya.
scenes.speak: Gaganyaan का budget लगभग double हो गया है: 2018 में 10000 करोड़ रुपये, फिर September 2024 में 20193 करोड़। और इसी बीच crewed flight का target 2021 से खिसक कर 2027 हो गया।

scenes.say: Ab woh idea jo yaad rakhna hai: satellite navigation ko 4 satellites kyun chahiye. Har satellite mein atomic clock hoti hai, aur woh lagataar time broadcast karta hai. Aapka receiver note karta hai ki signal kab pahuncha. Signal lagbhag 3 lakh kilometre per second ki speed se chalte hain. Toh travel time se distance nikal aata hai.
scenes.speak: अब वो idea जो याद रखना है: satellite navigation को 4 satellites क्यों चाहिए। हर satellite में atomic clock होती है, और वो लगातार time broadcast करता है। आपका receiver note करता है कि signal कब पहुँचा। Signal लगभग 3 लाख kilometre per second की speed से चलते हैं। तो travel time से distance निकल आता है।

scenes.say: Ek distance batata hai ki aap us satellite ke charon taraf ek bahut bade sphere par kahin hain. 2 spheres ek circle mein milte hain. Teesra use 2 points tak le aata hai, jinmein se sirf ek Earth ke paas hota hai. Lekin aapke phone ki clock sasti hai, atomic nahi. Uski galti ek chautha unknown hai, isliye chautha satellite chahiye.
scenes.speak: एक distance बताता है कि आप उस satellite के चारों तरफ़ एक बहुत बड़े sphere पर कहीं हैं। 2 spheres एक circle में मिलते हैं। तीसरा उसे 2 points तक ले आता है, जिनमें से सिर्फ़ एक Earth के पास होता है। लेकिन आपके phone की clock सस्ती है, atomic नहीं। उसकी ग़लती एक चौथा unknown है, इसलिए चौथा satellite चाहिए।

scenes.say: Chaliye try karte hain. Maan lijiye signal ko pahunchne mein zero point zero saat second lagta hai. 3 lakh kilometre per second guna zero point zero saat, yaani 21000 kilometre. Ab maan lijiye aapke phone ki clock ek second ke hazaarwe hisse se galat hai. Sirf itne se aapki location 300 kilometre khisak jaati hai.
scenes.show: A tiny clock slip, a 300 km error
scenes.speak: चलिए try करते हैं। मान लीजिए signal को पहुँचने में zero point zero सात second लगता है। 3 लाख kilometre per second गुना zero point zero सात, यानी 21000 kilometre। अब मान लीजिए आपके phone की clock एक second के हज़ारवें हिस्से से ग़लत है। सिर्फ़ इतने से आपकी location 300 kilometre खिसक जाती है।

scenes.say: Unknowns giniye: 3 aapki position ke liye, north south, east west aur height, aur 1 aapki clock ke liye. 4 unknowns ke liye 4 satellites chahiye, har ek se ek equation. Sirf 3 ke saath, jaise NVS zero three se pehle NavIC ke paas the, koi reliable fix nahi milta.
scenes.speak: Unknowns गिनिए: 3 आपकी position के लिए, north south, east west और height, और 1 आपकी clock के लिए। 4 unknowns के लिए 4 satellites चाहिए, हर एक से एक equation। सिर्फ़ 3 के साथ, जैसे NVS zero three से पहले NavIC के पास थे, कोई reliable fix नहीं मिलता।

scenes.say: Aapke liye iska matlab kya hai? NavIC trains, vehicles aur ships ko track karne mein madad karta hai, aur one nation, one time project se juda hai. Phir se 4 satellites ke saath, yeh poore India aur uske aas paas lagbhag 1500 kilometre tak fix de sakta hai. ISRO ke chairman ise ek strategic national asset kehte hain.
scenes.show: NavIC: trains, vehicles, ships, one time
scenes.speak: आपके लिए इसका मतलब क्या है? NavIC trains, vehicles और ships को track करने में मदद करता है, और one nation, one time project से जुड़ा है। फिर से 4 satellites के साथ, ये पूरे India और उसके आस पास लगभग 1500 kilometre तक fix दे सकता है। ISRO के chairman इसे एक strategic national asset कहते हैं।

scenes.say: Ek aam galatfehmi: Pakistan ke paas ab apna human spaceflight programme nahi hai. Uske paas na rocket hai, na crewed spacecraft. Uski flight se aap par seedha koi farak nahi padta. Gaganyaan se padta hai: uska 20000 crore rupaye ka budget public ka paisa hai.
scenes.show: Myth: Pakistan now has its own programme
scenes.image: Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission
scenes.speak: एक आम ग़लतफ़हमी: Pakistan के पास अब अपना human spaceflight programme नहीं है। उसके पास न rocket है, न crewed spacecraft। उसकी flight से आप पर सीधा कोई फ़र्क नहीं पड़ता। Gaganyaan से पड़ता है: उसका 20000 करोड़ रुपये का budget public का पैसा है।

scenes.say: Aage dekhiye Gaganyaan ki pehli uncrewed flight, jismein Vyommitra naam ka robot jayega. ISRO kehta hai at the earliest opportunity, yaani pehla mauka milte hi. India Today ki ek report kehti hai February 2027 se pehle nahi. Crewed flight ka target 2027 hai. Pakistan ka Jinnah 1 rover China ke Chang'e 8 par lagbhag 2028 mein jaana hai. Abhi pata nahi: Ali kitne din rukenge, aur India ki taraf se koi official reaction.
scenes.show: Uncrewed Gaganyaan: no firm date yet
scenes.speak: आगे देखिए Gaganyaan की पहली uncrewed flight, जिसमें Vyommitra नाम का robot जाएगा। ISRO कहता है at the earliest opportunity, यानी पहला मौका मिलते ही। India Today की एक report कहती है February 2027 से पहले नहीं। Crewed flight का target 2027 है। Pakistan का Jinnah 1 rover China के Chang'e 8 पर लगभग 2028 में जाना है। अभी पता नहीं: Ali कितने दिन रुकेंगे, और India की तरफ़ से कोई official reaction।

scenes.say: 3 baatein yaad rakhiye. Satellite navigation ko 4 satellites chahiye: 3 aapki jagah ke liye, 1 aapki clock ke liye. Pakistan ka astronaut China ke rocket par gaya, jabki India apna khud bana raha hai, dheere dheere. Aur Gaganyaan ki pehli uncrewed flight ki pakki date par nazar rakhiye.
scenes.show: Four satellites. Ride vs build. Watch Gaganyaan.
scenes.speak: 3 बातें याद रखिए। Satellite navigation को 4 satellites चाहिए: 3 आपकी जगह के लिए, 1 आपकी clock के लिए। Pakistan का astronaut China के rocket पर गया, जबकि India अपना ख़ुद बना रहा है, धीरे धीरे। और Gaganyaan की पहली uncrewed flight की पक्की date पर नज़र रखिए।

stories.headline: Dengue up 34-fold and record heat deaths as climate talks fail
stories.question: How is a warming planet spreading dengue and killing people in heatwaves?
stories.dek: Warmer, wetter weather helps the dengue mosquito spread, and hotter summers kill directly. Reported dengue has risen 34-fold since 1990, and England set a heat-death record just as COP31 ended without a deal.

so_far.text: Dengue is a virus spread mainly by the Aedes aegypti mosquito. It is endemic, meaning always present, in over 100 countries. The World Health Organization (WHO) says 2024 was the worst year on record, with 14.6 million reported cases and over 12,000 deaths. WHO lists rising temperatures, heavy rain, humidity, shifting mosquito ranges, urbanisation and strained health systems as drivers. Heat also kills directly. In July 2026 the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) counted 2,877 heat deaths in England in May and June alone, and warned 2026 could be a record.

what_happened.text: On 22 November COP31, the UN climate summit in Antalya, ended without a final agreement. Dozens of nations objected to a text that did not mention fossil fuels and gave no deal to raise money for poorer countries. On 24 November reports said UKHSA had recorded 5,258 heat-related deaths in summer 2026, the highest on record. The Guardian and BBC say England; Reuters says UK. On 25 November Nature reported a new analysis: reported dengue cases worldwide rose 34-fold, from about 430,000 in 1990 to 14.7 million in 2024. It is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed.

steps.text: Warming has widened the range of Aedes aegypti, the mosquito that mainly carries dengue, so it survives in more places.
Heat, heavy rain and humidity give mosquitoes more breeding water and longer seasons; India's season now runs beyond the post-monsoon months.
Growing cities pack more people near mosquitoes, so each infected mosquito can bite more people.
Heat also kills directly: England's 2026 summer saw 5,258 heat-related deaths, a record.
COP31 ended without new money, so adaptation such as early warnings in Nepal and island sea defences gets harder to fund.

history.text:
Dengue is not new. Its severe form, dengue haemorrhagic fever, was first documented in epidemics in Manila in 1953–54 and in Bangkok in 1958. Epidemics have returned across Southeast Asia ever since, often larger each time. That set the pattern: dengue comes back, and it grows.

Reported cases kept climbing: about 430,000 worldwide in 1990, and 505,430 in 2000 by WHO's count. A 2024 analysis of 21 countries estimated that climate change explained about 18% of dengue incidence in 1995–2014, or over 4.6 million extra infections. It is the nearest available measure of warming's share of the rise.

lesson.big_idea: A rise in reported cases mixes real spread with growing cities and better counting. Warming is one real driver; scientists estimate its share by comparing our world with a modelled world without warming.

steps.title: A fold rise is a ratio
steps.text: A fold rise is the new count divided by the old one. Reported dengue went from about 430,000 in 1990 to 14.7 million in 2024. 14.7 million ÷ 430,000 is about 34, so 34-fold.

steps.title: Reported is not real
steps.text: Counts include only cases someone tested and recorded. Better testing can push counts up even if infections do not rise. WHO says most infections still go unreported, and the new analysis does not split the two.

steps.title: Heat helps the mosquito
steps.text: Dengue spreads through the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Warming has widened where it can live, and heavy rain and humidity give it breeding water. In warmer air the virus also matures faster inside the mosquito, so it can pass it on sooner.

steps.title: Other drivers share the credit
steps.text: Growing cities pack people close to mosquitoes, and strained health systems miss outbreaks. So warming is one cause among several. To find its share, scientists compare the real world with a model of the same world without warming.

stories.headline: Riemann hypothesis: two claimed proofs, but neither is accepted yet
stories.question: Is the Riemann hypothesis really solved now that a human-written proof exists too?
stories.dek: Not yet. The AI-assisted proof passed computer checks, but nobody understands it yet. Problems were reported in the human-written proof within hours. Experts say both need careful checking.

so_far.text: On 20 November 2026 Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, announced a proof of the Riemann hypothesis that he found working with the AI model Claude. It is written in Lean, a language a computer can check step by step. On 21 November the Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative, the groups behind Lean and its shared maths library, said they had full confidence in it. Independent checking tools accepted it. But the proof is about 17 million lines long, and no human-readable version exists.

what_happened.text: On 25 November 2026 the journal Nature reported that two proofs, one AI-assisted and one human-written, had stunned mathematicians, and that experts say both need careful checking. The human-written one is by Alessandro Masullo, a Stanford postdoc. Ravi Vakil, a Stanford professor and president of the American Mathematical Society, posted it on 20 November, calling it 'all human, with no AI'. It runs to about 940 pages and targets the generalized Riemann hypothesis. About eight hours later, Vakil reported problems in it, some found with AI models. On 22 November he said it would be accepted only once all issues are resolved to the community's satisfaction.

steps.text: A proof is accepted when experts are sure every step is correct and understand why it works.
Lean's computer checks confirmed every step of Alpöge's proof, but only against Mathlib's written statement of the hypothesis.

history.text:
The story starts in 1859. Bernhard Riemann wrote a paper on how many primes lie below a given size. In it he proposed that all 'non-trivial zeros' of the zeta function have real part 1/2. This matters because the prime number theorem gives the average spread of primes. The hypothesis governs how far the real primes stray from that average.

In 1896 Hadamard and de la Vallée-Poussin, working separately, showed there are no zeros on the line where the real part is 1. That gave the first proofs of the prime number theorem, but not Riemann's sharper claim. In 1900 David Hilbert put the hypothesis on his list of problems, as number 8.

In 1976 Miller showed that a broader version, the generalized Riemann hypothesis, would give fast tests for whether a number is prime. In 2000 the Clay Mathematics Institute made the hypothesis one of seven Millennium Prize Problems, with a $1 million prize. In 2002 Agrawal, Kayal and Saxena built a fast prime test that needs no hypothesis at all.

Computers have checked the first 10 trillion zeros. But the hypothesis is about infinitely many zeros, so no finite check can settle it. Only a proof can. That is why two claimed proofs on 20 November 2026 caused such a stir.

lesson.concept: What a computer proof check can and cannot tell you
lesson.big_idea: A proof is a chain of small logical steps. A program like Lean can confirm every step is valid, but it cannot tell you why the result is true, or whether the statement is the one you meant.

steps.title: A proof is many small steps
steps.text: A proof starts from accepted facts and moves forward in small steps. Each step must follow from earlier ones by the rules of logic. One broken step breaks the whole proof.

steps.title: Humans check by reading
steps.text: Traditionally, expert readers called referees go through every step by hand. Long proofs take months or years. Masullo's 940-page draft took about 12 years to write, and problems were reported within hours of its release.

steps.title: Lean checks every step mechanically
steps.text: In Lean, each step is written in a strict computer language. A small core program, the kernel, checks each step without tiring. Independent checking tools accepted Alpöge's 17-million-line proof.

steps.title: The statement must be right
steps.text: A checker only proves what is written. If the written statement differs from the real hypothesis, the proof proves something else. So Lean's certification rests on Mathlib's statement being the intended one.

steps.title: Checked is not understood
steps.text: Mathematicians want to know why a result is true, so they can reuse the ideas. Explaining the new ideas in Alpöge's proof still lies ahead, and he plans a shorter readable version.

scenes.say: Yeh kyun important hai, yeh samajhne ke liye 1859 mein chaliye. Bernhard Riemann ne ek paper likha ki ek given size se neeche kitne primes hote hain. Unhone propose kiya ki zeta function ke saare so called non trivial zeros ka real part aadha hota hai.
scenes.show: 1859: every zero on the line ½
scenes.speak: यह क्यों important है, यह समझने के लिए 1859 में चलिए। Bernhard Riemann ने एक paper लिखा कि एक given size से नीचे कितने primes होते हैं। उन्होंने propose किया कि zeta function के सारे so called non trivial zeros का real part आधा होता है।

scenes.say: Zeros kyun matter karte hain? Prime number theorem batata hai ki primes average mein kaise faile hue hain. Riemann hypothesis yeh tay karta hai ki asli primes us average se kitna door bhatakte hain.
scenes.speak: Zeros क्यों matter करते हैं? Prime number theorem बताता है कि primes average में कैसे फैले हुए हैं। Riemann hypothesis यह तय करता है कि असली primes उस average से कितना दूर भटकते हैं।

scenes.say: Phir aaye turning points. 1896 mein Hadamard aur de la Vallee Poussin ne prime number theorem prove kiya, lekin Riemann ka zyada sharp claim nahi. 1900 mein David Hilbert ne ise apni problems ki list mein daala. 1976 mein Miller ne ek broader version ko fast prime testing se joda. Aur 2000 mein Clay Institute ne proof ke liye 1 million dollar ka inaam rakha.
scenes.speak: फिर आए turning points। 1896 में Hadamard और de la Vallee Poussin ने prime number theorem prove किया, लेकिन Riemann का ज़्यादा sharp claim नहीं। 1900 में David Hilbert ने इसे अपनी problems की list में डाला। 1976 में Miller ने एक broader version को fast prime testing से जोड़ा। और 2000 में Clay Institute ने proof के लिए 1 million dollar का इनाम रखा।
